title: The page builder's model and a built page's render
headline: The page model itself is lean: a stored page is about 340 bytes a block and a two-block page's own markup is 1.6 KB. The waste is in how pages are read, cached and wrapped: every storefront document carries the layout twice (27 KB), 45 of the demo store's 261 built entries keep a copy of every page of the store to find one page or one title, and all 261 carry one cache tag, so publishing one page makes the whole store's site render again. The owner filter `is not distinct from` cannot use an index (60,000 rows read to return 27 on a test table) and a five-minute job re-reads every published page of every site with chat on. None of this rests on a feature being unused: each cost grows with stores, pages or products, and each is cheapest to change before opening.

clean: Stored page JSON is sparse: 303 optional settings stay absent, per-size values exist only where set (101 B in the 10.5 KB Orbit home), pictures are addresses never data, and the limits hold (100 blocks, 50 rows, 50,000 characters of HTML). 35 fields have a default (mostly an empty string, null or an empty list) and those are written out; ids are 20% of a page.
No stored setting was found without a reader, but the scan behind this is a token match on key names and cannot prove it for every block.
A block's markup is lean: the two-block page's main is 1,583 B, the whole storefront document has one inline style attribute, and per-size differences are CSS classes, not duplicated markup.

Picture enrichment is batched and never saved: withPageAlts() reads alt texts and small copies for all pictures of the pages it is given in one query, and asks nothing for a page without pictures (src/server/media-alts.ts:26-55).

Page versions cost only when used: the same content is not stored again (md5 compare), a page keeps its newest 50, and the list reads titles only (src/server/page-versions.ts:22-45, src/lib/page-versions.ts:6). 50 whole copies is a product choice about how far back to go; it is paid per page that is edited that often.

Saving a page is one person's press: the builder has no autosave (no timer or debounce in src/components/admin/page-builder.tsx), and a draft save does not refresh the site's cache (pages/actions.ts:107).
Interactive block parts load only where drawn: 19 lazyView stand-ins in src/components/lazy/blocks.tsx; the page model is kept out of visitor scripts by a scan test (docs/performance.md).

Who sees a part costs nothing unless conditional, and then little: Always and Never are decided without a hole; a condition reads only the kinds of fact it asks about, each once per request (src/components/visible-part.tsx:16-27, src/server/visibility.ts:45-76).

A header or footer built in the builder is read as one row by its id (src/server/site-layouts.ts:28-45), and findPublishedPage() reads one row; a page at its own address keeps only itself in its resume state (1,155 B on /om-oss).

Content grids are capped at 48 items and cached by tag (src/server/content-grid.ts:278). A grid of pages or articles still reads each item's whole document for a card; PM-2's light read and PM-6's columns cover it.

The chat agent is off unless a store turns it on (chat_agents.enabled defaults to false), so the knowledge job does nothing for a store without chat; its waste is in what it repeats for those with it (PM-3).
The admin's English catalogue is no longer bundled as a fallback (D540, docs/performance.md:183), so the editor's inline texts (PM-10) are not a second copy of something in the scripts.
The page studio's prompt and patterns are small per call and run only when someone asks (judged clean by the AI dimension; nothing in this dimension contradicts it).

findings.title: Every storefront page renders and ships the whole layout twice, because the cart drawer's slot sits on the root layout
findings.evidence: Next's own code, read again in this pass: a root layout that has `children` and one more slot is wrapped in a boundary whose notFound value is the root layout drawn a second time around the not-found page (create-component-tree.js:551 and :659-670; its comment says it 'renders the RootLayout twice'). The market layout is a root layout and takes `drawer` (layout.tsx:104, :214). Re-run in this pass with the skeptic's script (work/pmsk/nf2.mjs) on two captures: 27,070 bytes reachable only through that value in /s/demo/no/om-oss (38.9% of its 69,548 B payload) and in the home page (31.6%); Kaizena Flow's own front page has no such copy. The copy holds the header (4.7 KB), the phone menu (3.7 KB), the footer (3.5 KB), the bottom bar (2.1 KB), the theme's CSS (1.8 KB) and the breakpoint sheet (1.76 KB). The per-request cart link is in both copies, and getCartCount() is not memoised (cart.ts:544), so the layout's per-request work runs twice. Counted here: 22 route folders and page.tsx sit under the layout; 26 files import from the folder through the alias (44 import lines); 17 test files name the folder. The drawer is a <dialog> opened with showModal (cart-drawer.tsx:60), so where it sits in the markup does not show.
findings.cost: 27 KB raw in every storefront document (0.7 to 1.3 KB gzip, about 0.3 KB Brotli, because it repeats), the same again in every layout segment file (54.7 KB against the page's 9.3 KB), and the header, footer, menus, the layout's per-request parts and the store's 404 page drawn a second time on each server render. A store with its own 404 page (not-found.tsx:19) ships that whole built page inside every page. Larger with a built header and footer: production's demo home is 203 KB with 149 KB of payload.
findings.who_pays: The server per render (most); a shopper's browser (parse and memory, little on the wire); the build

findings.title: Finding one page, or a title, loads every published page of the store with its whole content
findings.evidence: listPublishedPages() (pages.ts:664-679) selects `published` for every page of a type, runs the full schema on each, then asks the media library about every picture of every page. My rg: 36 lines outside tests (the definition and one comment among them), so 34 calls. 13 pick one page by id; others want slugs or titles. New in this pass: every product page calls it for one title, the back link to All products (p/[handle]/page.tsx:122 through productsPageOf). Measured on the build with my own script (work/pmplan/rdcall.mjs): 45 of the demo store's 261 prerendered entries keep the whole list in their resume state (all 30 product page entries, 9 blog, 3 products, 3 home), 117,432 bytes in all. The article list is the one that grows without limit: blog-listing.tsx:115 reads every article whole to learn which categories are used, and article-page.tsx:40 and :53 read every article whole for their addresses. Next's default cache for `use cache` is one 50 MB memory store per instance (config-shared.js:102), shared by every store's entries, and the guide says it does not usually persist between serverless requests (use-cache.md:247). Production: 79,778 calls, 29 rows a call, 781 s, the app's second most expensive statement; with no shoppers yet these are misses from deploys, crawlers and tests.
findings.cost: Per cache miss: every page's JSON from the database, about 0.9 ms of zod per realistic page (about 26 ms for a 29-page store, estimate) and one pictures query naming every picture of the store. Per hit: decoding the whole array. Per prerendered page that asks: a copy of all the store's pages in its resume state, so that grows with pages times product pages per store. Estimate: at production's average (29 pages of about 3.3 KB) one store's list is about 100 KB of the instance's 50 MB.
findings.who_pays: The database; the server per cold instance, per render and per resume; the build

findings.title: The five-minute knowledge job reads and parses every published page of every site with chat on, and re-cuts wordless pages for ever
findings.evidence: syncPageKnowledge() selects `p.published` for every published page and article with two sub-selects each (knowledge.ts:170-176), runs the full schema on each (:182) and only then compares versions (:187). A page that cuts to no passage (cutPassages returns [] for no text, lib/knowledge.ts:63-65) never gets a row to carry its version, so every run cuts it again: a transaction with a delete and no insert (:248-256). Production: that delete ran 91,200 times and removed 782 rows in all; the page statement ran about 24,100 times at about 40 whole pages a call; the job's last run took 542 ms, fourth slowest of 84. Read in this pass: an article's address needs only its blogId (blogOfArticle, lib/blogs.ts:54), so the comparison can be made without the document. A re-cut deletes the page's passages with their vectors, which the store's AI then makes again, so a change here must not re-cut what is already cut.
findings.cost: 542 ms of each five-minute run today, for one or two sites. It grows with sites with chat on times published pages, every 300 s, changed or not: 1,000 such stores of 30 pages would pull about 30,000 documents and spend about 25 s in zod each run (estimate from 0.9 ms a page), on top of about 7,000 statements run one after another.
findings.who_pays: The database; the server per scheduled run

findings.title: A product's layout is cached once per product, whole
findings.evidence: productLayoutFor(storeId, productId) is a `use cache` function, so its entry is keyed by the store and the product, and it returns the chosen layout's whole parsed content (product-layouts.ts:27-63). A store with one standard layout and K products therefore gets K entries holding the same document, K statements that each return it, K runs of the page schema and K picture lookups on a cold instance; and each product page's resume state keeps its own copy (in the build, demo-bordlampe.meta holds the entry: 15 bytes, null, because the demo store has no built layout). Each of the six signature themes ships a product layout (orbit.ts:452, :611). Measured here by bundling the themes (work/pmplan/layouts.mjs, layouts2.mjs): 1,362 to 1,504 bytes as written, 13 blocks in 2 rows; Orbit's is 1,485 bytes as stored and takes 0.2 ms to parse. So a store started from a launch theme has one from its first day.
findings.cost: About 1.5 KB per product of the instance's 50 MB cache (config-shared.js:102) and of each built product page's resume state, for a theme's layout; an owner's own layout of 10 KB makes it 10 KB a product (estimate). 2,000 products: 3 to 20 MB of one instance's 50 MB for copies of one document, plus 0.2 ms of parsing and one picture lookup per product page on a cold instance.
